answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a time-locked stake, like a bond, that is slashed when an agent is caught cheating. Think of a shared meadow where every grazing agent posts a deposit before entering: honest agents get it back with fees, while fake identities multiply the cost of the attack because each fake must fund its own bond. A fraud proof then acts like a plume of smoke signalling the violation, and the slashed stake drains into a common lagoon used to reimburse victims, so creating thousands of cheap fakes becomes expensive and self-defeating.
